Currently you can use `is_same()`, it does not produce errors on type mismatch. However, note that `is_same()` is stricter about types and references than the `==` operator.

Yeah it's more like a proposal but at the same time, I still feel like it's a design flaw ('bug') that the default equality operator can't take two variants and deal with it 'maturely'. I've come across comments in the other threads about how "comparing an object and a non-object almost certainly means you've made a mistake in your code" (operative word being 'almost') but I strongly disagree, and I don't think the core's default behavior should be to try to catch hypothetical errors that only match specific cases while causing issues for other people at the same time who are just trying to get very basic things done. The language shouldn't be made to try to preemptively help debug badly-written code.

Thanks for telling me about is_same(), it works for my use case, so that's one less hack I need to add to my toolbox! It's a shame is_same() feels like a hack added on top to fix the language, because honestly as far as I can tell it feels like a pretty logical definition for an equality operator in a non-pure language that uses references.

I'm wondering to which extent the code is hard to fix, given how easy at the time it was to implement this weird equality type-strictness. As I said I don't see how it could cause issues in terms of backward compatibility to just return false instead of 'failure' when two values of different types are compared, since nobody can have code that relies on that behavior, since you can't catch errors and therefore can't rely on their existence to design the logic of your code (unless I'm missing something?). Some people even mentioned replacing exception throwing with a simple warning that could be muted, that feels like a good compromise (even though I personally don't see the point of a warning) for those who would somehow rely on the code throwing errors when trying to compare values of different types...
Same problem. I think it's obviously should return `false` if Object compared with not Object.
